title: Networks
description: Declare storage-sync, compute and serving networks, attach them to nodes or node labels, and see which interface each node resolves to.
fallbackNote: Dedicated networks come first. A role without one is carried by the management network: serving goes through the agent tunnel, storage sync and compute traffic use the address the node reaches the server from. Switch these roles off per node on the node's Networks tab.

actions.confirmDelete: Delete network {{name}}? Running instances keep the network they started with.

form.name: Name
form.rolesHint: Select all three for an all-in-one network. Internal testing covers storage sync and compute networks.
form.typeHint: Only nodes on the same network are treated as reachable.
form.cidrHint: Traffic uses the interface whose address is in this subnet.
form.selectorNote: The selector is only a default: a node attachment can override the interface, IP and HCAs. With both CIDR and interface name filled in, both must match.
form.bootstrapCidrHint: Only when the inferred bootstrap does not fit: the handshake (NCCL out-of-band, vLLM master address) uses the interface in this subnet; data still goes over the HCAs.
form.interfaceHint: Only needed when the subnet alone is ambiguous. A node attachment can override it.
form.rdmaInferred: Nothing to fill in: once nodes are attached, each node's bootstrap IP, HCAs and HCA IPs are inferred. You can then add or remove HCAs in the node list.
form.acceleratorInferred: No selector is needed: once nodes are attached, each node's rails are the accelerator cards whose port is up and has an address, and you can add or remove cards in the node list. The handshake uses a host address (the management address by default); data moves on the cards' ports.
form.acceleratorBootstrapCidrHint: For the handshake only (HCCL rootInfo, MASTER_ADDR): it moves to the host interface inside this subnet. Data moves on the cards' ports, which are not in this subnet.
form.roleNotOnType: Accelerator RDMA carries compute traffic only: host processes cannot bind the address of a card's port, so storage sync and serving cannot use it.
form.typeHelp: Host Ethernet is TCP on a host interface. Host RDMA uses the host's RDMA ports, InfiniBand or RoCE as read from each node's ports. Accelerator RDMA uses the RoCE ports on the accelerator cards themselves (Ascend NPUs), one rail per card. The type decides the NCCL/UCX/HCCL settings and device injection.

detail.noNodes: No node resolves to this network yet
detail.rdmaInferredHelp: Each node uses its fastest active RDMA ports (a RoCE port needs an IPv4 address on its interface) as HCAs, and the first HCA's interface address as bootstrap; InfiniBand without IPoIB uses the management address.
detail.acceleratorInferredHelp: Each node's rails are the accelerator cards whose port is up and has an address. The bootstrap is the host address the handshake uses, the management address by default; data moves on the cards' ports.
detail.title: Network details
detail.rdmaEditHint: Add or remove HCAs, or change the bootstrap, per node below.
detail.acceleratorEditHint: Add or remove cards, or change the bootstrap, per node in the table below.

attach.modeHint: Node attachments outrank label attachments; within the same rank the earlier attachment wins.
attach.ipPlaceholder: Leave empty to use the interface's address
attach.rdmaInferred: Each node's bootstrap IP and HCAs are inferred once attached.

warning.conflict: Several {{role}} networks reach this node at the same rank. {{winner}} was attached first and is used; not used: {{losers}}. Attach one of them to this node directly to choose explicitly.
warning.override_missing: Override {{value}} ({{kind}}) is not in the node's last reported inventory.
warning.summary: {{count}} node(s) have warnings; open the details to see why.
warning.link_layer_mismatch: Nodes on this network resolved to different link layers ({{link_layers}}). InfiniBand and RoCE cannot form one fabric; split them into separate networks.
warning.rdma_no_hca: No usable RDMA port: ports are down, or a RoCE port's interface has no IPv4 address.
warning.bootstrap_missing: No bootstrap address was resolved, so the handshake cannot reach this node.

node.none: No network is attached to this node.
node.notReported: This agent has not reported a network inventory yet.
node.acceleratorHint: RoCE ports on the cards themselves; the host does not list them as interfaces

forward.title: Serving network forwarder
forward.hint: The gateway connects here with TLS and a per-instance token. A node on a serving network is only reached over it: when the address is unreachable, requests to its instances fail, and new instances are not started there.

test.what: Every ordered pair of nodes connects from its address on this network to the peer's address on a fresh port and, optionally, streams data for a few seconds. Pairs run in rounds, one stream in and out per node at a time.
test.rdmaNote: TCP runs over the bootstrap interface. Choose RDMA bandwidth to measure the RDMA ports.
test.unsupported: Serving networks are reached from the server, not between nodes, so they have no internal test.
test.none: No test has run on this network yet.
test.interrupted: The test started {{time}} was interrupted before it finished.
test.slow: Under a tenth of the fastest pair in this run, likely across a slower link.
test.toolMissing: These nodes have no ib_write_bw, so their pairs will fail: {{nodes}}. Install perftest (for example apt install perftest) and wait for the next node report.
test.toolReady: Every node reported ib_write_bw. Each pair runs one ib_write_bw per rail in parallel and sums the rails.

patternHint.mesh: Every node probes every other node: N×(N−1) pairs, slow on large networks.
patternHint.ring: Nodes form a ring by name and each probes the next: N pairs in one round. It finds a bad node or HCA, not a break only between non-adjacent nodes.

test.retestHint: Run the test again after removing an HCA to see the new result.
test.partialHint: Some HCAs failed; click to see each HCA
test.noBootstrap: These nodes have no bootstrap address and their pairs will fail: {{nodes}}.
test.noAddress: These nodes have no address on this network and their pairs will fail: {{nodes}}.
test.noRails: These nodes have no usable HCA and their pairs will fail: {{nodes}}.

error.no_address: {{node}} has no address on this network (the bootstrap address on RDMA networks)
error.no_roce_v2_gid: This RoCE port on {{node}} has no IPv4 address on its interface, so no RoCE v2 connection
error.no_peer_rail: This HCA on {{node}} has no HCA to pair with on the other node
error.listener_failed: {{node}} could not open the test port: {{detail}}
error.bandwidth_failed: Reachable, but the throughput test failed: {{detail}}

test.acceleratorNote: The TCP test uses the bootstrap interface: it checks the host addresses the handshake uses, not the cards' ports.

cardNote.card_ping: The same-named accelerator cards of two nodes ping each other (npu3 to npu3). Good for routine checks and for confirming a network wired card to card.
cardNote.card_matrix: Every accelerator card of one node pings every card of the other. Which card reaches which cannot be read from the addresses; this measures it when the network is set up.

cardPatternHint.mesh: Every two nodes are tested once (a ping is answered, so one probe proves both directions): N×(N−1)÷2 pairs.
cardPatternHint.ring: Nodes are ordered by name in a circle and each tests the next: N pairs. Every pair of neighbours gets a complete result; a break that only shows between nodes that are not neighbours goes unseen.

test.cardEstimate: {{nodes}} nodes, {{pairs}} pairs: {{probes}} probes in {{rounds}} rounds, at most {{duration}}. A card sends one ping at a time, so a round lasts one probe's time limit at most.

card.openHint: Click a cell to see each pair of cards
card.odd: Node pairs that differ from the rest ({{count}}): {{pairs}}. This is usually the wiring or configuration fault to find.

matrix.full: Every card reaches every card: any combination of cards can be used.
matrix.diagonal: Cards reach their namesake only: a deployment must pick the same card numbers on both ends.
matrix.mixed: The wiring is irregular: open each node pair to see which cards reach which, and pick cards accordingly.
matrix.none: No pair of cards is reachable: check the links and addresses of the accelerator ports.
matrix.untested: No pair of cards was tested: see the reason on each node pair below.

ping.full: All same-named cards reach each other.
ping.diagonal: All same-named cards reach each other.
ping.mixed: Some same-named cards do not reach each other: open each node pair to see which.
ping.none: No same-named cards reach each other: check the links and addresses of the accelerator ports, or run a full card matrix to see whether they are cross-wired.
ping.untested: No pair of cards was tested: see the reason on each node pair below.

management.name: Management network

intro.title: About the management network
intro.source: Source: derived from the address each node reaches the server from; every node is on it.
intro.fixed: Fixed: it cannot be edited or deleted, and needs no attaching.
intro.roles: Roles: it carries a role on a node that has no dedicated network for it. Switch that off per node in the table below or on the node's Networks tab.

management.selector: Address the node reaches the server from
management.title: Management network
management.notReported: The agent has not reported its management address yet; upgrade the agent.
management.remote: Source address seen by the server
management.roleHint: Dedicated networks come first; these switches only matter where a node has none for the role. When off: serving — no new instances on this node; storage sync — download from the image or model source only; compute traffic — multi-node deployments are refused. Applies to new instances only.

bulk.title: Bulk edit
bulk.confirm: Change the management network roles of the {{count}} selected nodes? Applies to new instances only.
bulk.label: Bulk edit selected nodes

roleTip.serving: Inference requests reach this node over the agent tunnel. Where the node has no dedicated serving network, turning this off places no new instance on it.
roleTip.storage_sync: Nodes copy models and images to each other directly. Where the node has no dedicated storage-sync network, turning this off makes it download from the image or model source only.
roleTip.compute: Traffic between nodes in multi-node inference. Where the node has no dedicated compute network, turning this off leaves it out of multi-node deployments.

management.switchIntro: Each switch decides whether this traffic takes the management network when the node has no dedicated network for it
management.switchEffect: Changes apply to instances created afterwards; running instances are not affected. A role a dedicated network already carries is marked next to its switch.

monitor.scope: One line per node, counted on this network's interface and HCAs on that node.
monitor.errorsHint: NIC errors and drops, RDMA errors and CNPs
monitor.roleHint: All of the node's traffic for this role (rx + tx)
monitor.computeEthernet: Compute traffic over Ethernet cannot be told apart in NIC counters; it is part of the NIC totals.
monitor.acceleratorNote: Traffic on the accelerator ports does not pass through host interfaces; these charts show the bootstrap interface only.

topology.title: Network topology and settings
topology.description: Two typical deployments: which network each kind of traffic takes, and where each setting is made and what it does. The numbers on the diagram match the table below; point at a number or a table row to highlight its lines.

diagram.tunnelVia: through the agent tunnel to the instance

simple.heading: Simple: the management network carries everything, compute has its own
simple.summary: The server has one listen address that operators, inference clients and nodes all reach. The management network carries serving and storage sync on its own; only multi-node inference needs a compute network.

1.name: Console listen address
1.where: Settings → Listen addresses (listen.console in server.yaml); restart to apply
1.does: The IP:port this server accepts connections on. Node access and the inference API use it too unless set separately
1.not: The address others use to reach the server: browsers use the one in the address bar, nodes the one in their install command; reverse proxies and NAT work

2.name: Management network
2.where: Nothing to set. Node detail → Networks → Management network, or Networks → Management network, can turn off roles per node
2.does: The local address an agent reaches the server from. Without a dedicated network it carries serving (through the agent tunnel), storage sync (node to node) and compute traffic
2.not: Cannot be deleted or re-addressed; roles with a dedicated network do not use it

3.name: Compute network (RDMA)
3.where: Networks → Create network, role Compute, type RDMA, attached to nodes or a node label
3.does: NCCL / RDMA traffic of multi-node inference and KV transfer of disaggregated prefill/decode; a deployment's nodes must share one compute network
3.not: Carries no serving or storage sync; falls back to the management network (Ethernet) with a warning when not all nodes of a group are on it

complex.heading: Complex: a dedicated network per kind of traffic
complex.summary: The console and management API listen on the office network and the inference API on the business network; the server and compute nodes share a dedicated management network, inference requests take a dedicated serving network, and nodes have dedicated storage sync and compute networks.

1.name: Console listen address
1.where: Settings → Listen addresses (listen.console); restart to apply
1.does: Serves the console and management API only on these local addresses
1.not: The address operators use (a proxy or NAT on the office network works)

2.name: Inference API listen address
2.where: Settings → Listen addresses → Advanced (listen.gateway); restart to apply
2.does: Answers /v1 only on these local addresses, keeping inference traffic apart from management
2.not: The address clients use; integration examples use the browser's current address

3.name: Node access listen address
3.where: Settings → Listen addresses → Advanced (listen.agent); restart to apply
3.does: Accepts agent connections only on these local addresses, for example only on the management network
3.not: The address nodes dial: the --server in the install command, kept in the agent's config; before changing this, make sure that address still forwards here

4.name: Management network
4.where: Nothing to set. Node detail → Networks → Management network, or Networks → Management network, switches roles per node
4.does: The local address an agent reaches the server from (eth0 here). Carries any role that has no dedicated network
4.not: Here serving, storage sync and compute all have dedicated networks, so it carries only the control plane

5.name: Serving network
5.where: Networks → Create network, role Serving, attached to nodes
5.does: The gateway sends inference requests straight to port 19443 (TLS) on the node's serving IP, not through the agent tunnel; it probes once before an instance goes live and fails if unreachable
5.not: Not the address clients use (that is ②); never falls back to the tunnel

6.name: Storage sync network
6.where: Networks → Create network, role Storage sync, attached to nodes
6.does: Nodes copy models and images directly, over a network both ends of a pair share
6.not: Downloads from registries and model hubs take the node's default route, unaffected

7.name: Compute network
7.where: Networks → Create network, role Compute, type RDMA, attached to nodes
7.does: NCCL / RDMA of multi-node inference and disaggregated KV transfer; the RDMA type injects devices and NCCL_IB_HCA and similar variables
7.not: Bootstrap handshakes use its IP interface (eth0 here); data uses the IB ports

8.name: Compute node address
8.where: Entered when adding a node (SSH-managed or server-dial mode)
8.does: The server connects to the host: installs or recovers the agent over SSH, or dials the connection in server-dial mode
